note: Investigation results for each pre-registered falsifier, plus additional findings surfaced beyond the minimum set (the dispatch's 'go beyond it' instruction). Full detail and severity ranking in the findings report; this checkpoint records the raw evidence trail.

attackSurface1_crosswalk.positiveResult: 60 genuinely random crosswalked Williamson pairs (ORDER BY md5(r_prop_id||seed), not owner-curated) checked against legal_description: 60/60 show clear subdivision/lot correlation, including several with disagreeing owner_name (real ownership-transfer noise, not mis-joins). The mechanism holds under adversarial third-derivation testing.
attackSurface1_crosswalk.defectFoundByADifferentAngle: The uniqueness gate (count(*) OVER PARTITION BY target_prop_id = 1) only guards fan-out FROM the R-row's perspective, never checks whether the R-side situs itself is shared by multiple R-accounts. Live query (180s timeout, succeeded): 4,558 situs addresses shared by 2+ R-prefix accounts; 134 of those groups (777 accounts) also have a unique numeric-roll match, exposing them to a many-to-one collision. Confirmed manifested live: 48491:R664999 and 48491:R665023 both carry improvementValue=613956 (byte-identical), traced to shared address '1428 TREASURE MAP VW, LEANDER, TX 78641' and confirmed via legal_description (both S13718 - PALMERA BLUFF SECS 7 & 8) that this is a real developer/builder-phase CAD-account duplication, not coincidence.

attackSurface2_cadNull.structuralScopingConfirmed: Read ingest-existing.ts directly. ingestCadOntoRecords has `if (!cad) continue;` before applyCadScalar; applyCadScalar is the sole caller of stampAbsent, which is the sole caller of cadNullVerified. Neither is exported. Join-miss unreachability confirmed by code read, not just by trusting the fixtures.
attackSurface2_cadNull.typeExhaustionGapConfirmed: hasText/isCadNullText are exhaustive for string and null inputs (mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive by construction) but neither fires for a text[] (array) input -- confirmed by the module's own comment ('An unexpected type (e.g. text[] exemption_codes) is not a CAD null'). Live-sized (60s timeout, succeeded): exemptionCodes is live (503,780 absent-verified, correctly emitted for NULL cases) with 477,625/981,405 (48.7%) unaccounted -- populated arrays never stamp. Same mechanism confirmed by code read (not independently re-measured live, given timeout pressure) for landUseSource/acreageMethod: both stamped only inside their positive branch, no stampAbsent counterpart in the null branch.
attackSurface2_cadNull.positiveResult_taxYearGuard: cadNullVerified's null/blank tax_year refusal is effectively dead code against the live schema (cad_property.tax_year is integer NOT NULL) but was the exact mechanism that surfaced R6B's starved-input bug (CAD_ROWS_SQL omitting tax_year from its SELECT list produced undefined tax_year on every row, correctly triggering total refusal rather than a fabricated basis).

attackSurface3_publishGate.dormantConfirmed: grep -rn 'evaluatePublishGate|assertPublishableCounty' across hauska-factory/src/jobs/*.mjs and cloudbuild.*.yaml: exactly one call site, parcel-record-fill.mjs:900, inside a --poison-place-flagged branch of the job's sample-mode path (small selection.propIds, not a county-wide run). No cloudbuild job, CI step, or scheduled task invokes it against the live store. RAIL_LIVENESS_SQL (the module's own documented global-liveness SQL contract) has zero call sites in hauska-factory outside its own test file.
attackSurface3_publishGate.meaningVsPresence: evaluatePublishGate (read directly, publish-gate.ts) checks isUnaccounted(state) only -- a presence-shaped check with no ability to detect a wrong-but-present value like the attackSurface1 collision. Ties directly to finding #9 in the report.

attackSurface4_blindRederivation.naAuditInvariant: zoningDistrict's not-applicable count (370,289, live query, 100s timeout succeeded) exactly matches an independently-counted current unincorporated total (370,289, live query, 20s timeout succeeded) -- the NA-audit invariant the gap ledger's section 2 proved still holds post-session.
attackSurface4_blindRederivation.crosswalkMatchCount: Re-derived WILLIAMSON_CROSSWALK_SQL's exact logic from scratch (not copy-pasted) against the full 282,569 R-row population, 180s timeout, succeeded: 257,604 uniquely matched -- exact match to R1-crosswalk's design prediction, independently confirmed.
attackSurface4_blindRederivation.storeContentionCaveat: A full store-wide unaccounted count (60s, via the dedicated partial index) and a 39-rail batched liveness EXISTS check (15s) both timed out -- a genuinely broader re-derivation of the gap ledger's census table was not completed. See finding #8.

attackSurface5_r1bResidue.mechanism: parcel_record holds 282,570 Williamson records (30s timeout, succeeded), not 282,569 -- the extra row is 48491:PRIVATE ROAD, a real non-R-prefix landing/CAD account outside the crosswalk's scope by construction. It goes through the ordinary identity-join CAD path: cad_property row exists with tax_year=2025 but null improvement/land/assessed values, so cad-null-verified correctly emits absent-verified (confirmed live, 60s timeout succeeded). At the R1B checkpoint (before R6-cadnull was vendored), the same cell was unaccounted, accounting for the +1. Both R1's and R1B's numbers were internally correct; the gap was a scope mismatch (R-prefix-only prediction vs county-wide measurement), not data loss or a mis-join.

attackSurface7_process.newFindingBeyondMinimumSet: The PARCEL-R2-JURIS-STAMP cross-session collision (peer session misread REFUSED as GRANTED, pushed unauthorized code, had live Cloud Run executions racing against the corrected re-run for 2-3 minutes on two of six counties) -- read from that close's own incident report, not re-investigated independently. Elevated to the headline process finding: the queue's claim mechanism is a convention, not a structural lock; no check exists that a Cloud Run execution's invoking identity holds a currently-valid claim at execution start time.
attackSurface7_process.leaseLapseConfirmed: Same close's own OPEN note: this lane's own claim TTL lapsed during the incident response; the close was filed and treated as authoritative by convention, with the queue's bookkeeping left unreconciled.
attackSurface7_process.staleDispatchPattern: Confirmed as a working-but-reactive control (addenda demonstrably saved PARCEL-R6B-REINGEST from running against a superseded Williamson-deferral premise) -- not a structural guarantee, since it depends on the planner noticing drift before a card claims.
